C-REFLECT-SESSION-PART-EXTRACTOR.Summary: Adapt the vv-reflect session-graph extractor to the post-2026-11-25 part store in both operating modes: the single-session tree joins tool entries and assistant text from session_part for rows whose inline content is empty, and the archive aggregate adds session_part tool calls to the existing call union by call id, restoring friction signals, changed files, and message tails for post-migration sessions.
C-REFLECT-SESSION-PART-EXTRACTOR.Problem: OpenCode's 2026-11-25 storage migration moved message parts into session_part while assistant session_message rows persist with content=[]. The session-graph extractor — vv-reflect's mechanical pre-pass for friction signals — reads tool entries and text only from inline session_message content (plus the legacy part union for old sessions), so it is blind on the current host. Measured with the shipped extractor on 2026-11-25: a fully post-migration session that performed dozens of tool calls reports tool_calls=0, errors=0, test_runs=0, no changed files, and an empty message tail, while a pre-migration session reports 509 tool calls, 11 errors, 49 test runs, 20 changed files, and a populated tail. The single-session tree and the --archive machine-wide aggregate share the blindness, so $vv-reflect reports no friction for exactly the newest sessions it exists to reflect on.

Goals.Goal: In tree mode, assistant session_message rows whose data.content is empty take their tool entries and text from session_part: tool entries are the row's type='tool' parts and text is the joined type='text' parts, both keyed by message_id and ordered by ordinal; rows with non-empty inline content keep using it, so transition-era rows cannot duplicate.

In archive mode, archive_calls reads session_part tool rows (session_id, data with id/name/state) and adds each call to the existing union by call id only when that id is not already present from session_message or the legacy part table, preserving the established session_message-wins precedence.
The extractor docstring's storage model names all three stores — legacy part, inline session_message content, and post-migration session_part — instead of the current two-store description.

The synthetic-schema suite in src/lib/session-graph.test.ts gains post-migration coverage for both modes: a tree fixture whose assistant rows carry empty content with session_part parts (tool counts, edit-not-read file collection, tail text, reasoning excluded) and an archive fixture whose calls are counted from session_part.
A live smoke re-run of the measured sessions shows non-zero tool calls, populated files, and a non-empty tail for the post-migration session, recorded as change-time evidence in the bundle.

Constraints.Constraint: The extractor stays read-only (as_uri mode=ro connection, query_only) with a minimal diff; pre-migration and legacy-era output is unchanged, pinned by the existing fixtures.
The call-id union precedence is preserved exactly: session_message inline entries win, the legacy part table follows, session_part fills only ids absent from both.
No changes to the project_history.py extractor (owned by C-SESSION-PART-EXTRACTOR), no changes to the vv-reflect SKILL.md workflow, and no archive output-schema changes.
README and the M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS graph and V-M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS verification projections are reconciled inside this change's lifecycle, not retroactively.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No changes to the workflow engine, managed-skill delivery machinery, or unrelated managed skills and references.
No archive output reshaping, no new filters or metrics, and no streaming/pagination changes.
No investigation of V2 todo storage or of user-row parts (user text stays inline in the current host generation).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-01: For a tree-mode session whose assistant rows have empty inline content and whose parts live in session_part, tool_stats report the session_part tool calls (counts, errors, test-run classification) and changed_files list the mutating tools' state.input paths, with non-mutating tools excluded.
AC-02: For the same session, the message tail contains the assistant text joined from session_part type='text' parts, in message order, while reasoning and tool parts contribute no tail text.
AC-03: Pre-migration sessions (inline content) and legacy-era sessions (part-table union) produce identical output to before this change, pinned by the existing test fixtures.

AC-04: In archive mode, calls from session_part are counted once per call id, only for ids absent from session_message inline entries and the legacy part table; sessions without session_part rows keep their previous aggregates.
AC-05: The extractor docstring describes the three-store model accurately.
AC-06: src/lib/session-graph.test.ts covers AC-01, AC-02, and AC-04 deterministically with synthetic post-migration fixtures, python3-gated, alongside the unchanged existing fixtures.

AC-07: A live smoke run of the shipped extractor over the measured post-migration session returns non-zero tool calls, a non-empty files list, and a non-empty tail, recorded in the bundle's smoke-evidence.md.
AC-08: bun run check, bun run build, and bun run pack:check pass, and the grace lint baseline, target, and final assertion gates for this change pass with fresh runs.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The extended synthetic suite demonstrates post-migration extraction in both modes with the existing fixtures unchanged as regression pins. The live smoke run restores the measured signals for the post-migration session (previously zero across the board). The full gate stack and the grace assertion gates pass fresh. Deterministic tests assert extraction behavior against fixed schemas, not model behavior.

Assumptions.Assumption: session_part tool rows carry the call id in data.id with name and state shaped like inline content entries, and session_part rows expose session_id directly; verified on the live database on 2026-11-25.
The path.as_uri() connection already percent-encodes the database path, so no URI hardening is needed here, unlike the project_history.py predecessor.
The archive aggregate needs only call-level data from session_part; it carries no per-session message tails, so no archive tail work exists.
This stage was directed as measure, specify, plan, execute, review, and merge in one flow; the spec and plan are approved by that directive and no implementation precedes the bundle's baseline gate.
